# Peer review: Constructively reviewing data analysis projects

:::{.callout-important}
## Earlier than normal deadline

Deadline: **Thursday, December 11, 2025 at 6PM.**
:::

In this assignment, you will get to practice peer review of a data analysis project by reviewing a data analysis project created by your classmates. You will be writing your review in an issue in your assigned repository. You will be evaluated on the thoughtfullness and usefullness of your feedback in the review.

### Initiate a review request

- Before (or at the beginning of) the lab, every individual will initiate a peer review by opening an issue in the [UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025](https://github.com/UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025.git) repository. When opening the issue, select the "Peer Review Submission" issue template.
Thenn fill in the issue template with the required information. You can find the names of who was assigned to review your project [here][peer_review].

:::{.callout-note}
## For Section 2
Since our labs are later in the week we will do these instructions in a different order:

Each student will:

1. Go to the review repository: [UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025](https://github.com/UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025.git) repository
2. Create a new issue. Make sure the group you are reviewing is in the title of the issue so people can search and filter issues by group number
3. Fill out the review checklist for the group you are assigned to.
4. This issue is the URL you will submit for grading the peer review
:::

### Reviewing (individual)

-   Once an issue is assigned to you, you can start your review. You can view the project number you were assigned [here][peer_review]. If nothing is assigned to you before your lab session, please contact the team whose package you are assigned to review.
-   Using the review checklist linked to below, review the data analysis project assigned to you and write your comprehensive review.
    -   [MDS data analysis checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-checklist/main/data-analysis-review-checklist.md)
-   Other than checking the boxes in the template, we ask you to give at least 3 pieces of constructive feedback in the `Review Comments` section. It is OK to have some overlap with the other people reviewing the data analysis project, but there should be **at least 2 points of constructive feedback unique to each review**.
-   We encourage discussion and conversation between the authors and reviewers in the issue.
-   Each team will get a chance to address your comments!

:::{.callout-note}
## For Section 2
Since our labs are later in the week we will do these instructions in a different order:

You will not be explicitly assigned an issue by your reviewer.
You can filter the list of issues from [UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025](https://github.com/UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025.git) and assign yourself an issue if it helps you track where to look.

What you can do is create separate issues for topics you plan to address in your own group project repository, and use the issue links in  [UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025](https://github.com/UBC-MDS/data-analysis-review-2025.git) in your own group repository issue. This will cross link the issues so you can track everythig you need in your own repository.
:::

### Some guidance when you write your reviews

-   Be concrete and specific: support your claims with evidence: provide an example or point to specific things when you write comments.

-   Be empathetic: when you write feedback, try to put yourself at the receiving end and think about what feedback would have been useful for you.

-   Be Constructive: Do not use evaluative or judgmental language; instead be constructive and help them build on their strengths.

-   Tone: Don't be mean. A good test to determine whether you are being mean or not is putting yourself or a close friend at the receiving end or imagining whether you can say it to them in a face-to-face conversation.

## Submission Instructions

Follow the instructions for submission on Gradescope.
Enter these into Gradescope directly: there is no PDF to make.
You will submit:

1.  your GitHub.com username
2.  the URL of the issue containing your peer review (ideally linked to your post)
